evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from anatomical connectivity patterns.

claim: The VTNg innervates a number of other sites, including the lateral hypothalamus, preoptic area, medial septum, parts of the reticular pontine nucleus, median raphe nuclei, supramammillary nucleus and ventral tegmental area.
source_text: The VTNg does, however, innervate a number of other sites, including the lateral hypothalamus, preoptic area, medial septum, parts of the reticular pontine nucleus, median raphe nuclei, supramammillary nucleus and ventral tegmental area (Petrovicky, 1973; Leichnetz et al., 1989; Hayakawa et al., 1993)
evidence_reasoning: This is anatomical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Other VTNg efferents appear light and in some instances have not been confirmed.
source_text: These other VTNg efferents appear light (see Hayakawa and Zyo, 1984), and in some instances not been confirmed (Barone et al., 1981; Vertes, 1988)
evidence_reasoning: This is anatomical knowledge with some uncertainty, supported by citations.

claim: Lesions of alternative VTNg projection sites rarely result in the pattern of spatial memory impairments seen following VTNg lesions.
source_text: However, lesions of these alternative sites rarely result in the pattern of spatial memory impairments seen following VTNg lesions (e.g., Sarihi et al., 2000; Pan and McNaughton, 2002)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to prior lesion studies.

claim: The lack of Fos changes in the supramammillary and septal nuclei following VTNg lesions provides evidence that they are not having their effects via these routes.
source_text: In addition, the lack of Fos changes in the supramammillary and septal nuclei following VTNg lesions provides some evidence that they are not having their effects via these routes
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the c-Fos data showing no changes in these regions.

claim: The striking similarity of the VTNg and MTT lesion effects provides support for the VTNg-MB pathway.
source_text: while the striking similarity of the VTNg and MTT lesion effects in the present study provides further support for the VTNg-MB pathway
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the parallel behavioral and c-Fos effects of the two lesion types.

claim: The MTT and VTNg lesion effects appear to be selective for spatial working memory and not due to non-specific effects such as loss of arousal or motivation.
source_text: In rats, the MTT and VTNg lesion effects appear to be selective for spatial working memory and not due to non-specific effects such as loss of arousal or motivation.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the selective pattern of impairments and sparing on the geometric discrimination task.

claim: Both MTTx and VTNx groups were able to acquire a geometric discrimination task at the same rate, and to the same level, as the Sham group.
source_text: Both MTTx and VTNx groups were able to acquire a geometric discrimination task at the same rate, and to the same level, as the Sham group.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by the water-maze behavioral data.

claim: The geometric discrimination task may be particularly sensitive to lesions within the head-direction system.
source_text: This task may be particularly sensitive to lesions within the head-direction system (Aggleton et al., 2009; Vann, 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to prior work on this task.

claim: The MTT lesions in the present study are most likely to disconnect the medial MB efferents, while leaving many lateral MB efferents largely intact.
source_text: As the MTT lesions in the present study are most likely to disconnect the medial MB efferents, while leaving many lateral MB efferents largely intact (Vann and Albasser, 2009)
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from anatomical knowledge and supported by citation.

claim: The sparing of geometric discrimination performance provides support for the dissociation of two memory systems within the MBs.
source_text: this sparing provides further support for the dissociation of two memory systems within the MBs (Allen and Hopkins, 1989; Vann and Aggleton, 2004)
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the selective pattern of impairments and supported by prior theoretical work.

claim: Clinical studies show that both the MBs and the MTT are important for human memory.
source_text: Clinical studies show that both the MBs and the MTT are important for human memory, and recollective memory in particular (Dusoir et al., 1990; Van der Werf et al., 2000; Carlesimo et al., 2007; Tsivilis et al., 2008; Vann et al., 2009)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to clinical studies.

claim: The situation regarding the human VTNg is far less clear.
source_text: The situation regarding the human VTNg is far less clear.
evidence_reasoning: This acknowledges a gap in knowledge about the human VTNg.

claim: For a number of years the very existence of the VTNg in humans had been in doubt.
source_text: Indeed, for a number of years the very existence of this nucleus in humans had been in doubt (Petrovicky, 1971; Hayakawa and Zyo, 1983)
evidence_reasoning: This is historical knowledge about the field, supported by citations.

claim: The structure and connections of the VTNg are remarkably similar across species.
source_text: However, it is now apparent that the structure and connections of the VTNg are remarkably similar across species (Petrovicky, 1973; Irle and Markowitsch, 1982; Hayakawa and Zyo, 1984; Huang et al., 1992; Saunders et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This is comparative anatomical knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: There is only one reported amnesic patient with restricted damage in the VTN area.
source_text: To date, there is only one reported amnesic patient with restricted damage in the VTN area, but this study is limited in that only CT images were available (Goldberg et al., 1981)
evidence_reasoning: This is a factual statement about the clinical literature, supported by citation.

claim: The current findings support a novel model of limbic brain interactions.
source_text: The current findings support a novel model of limbic brain interactions.

claim: The MBs have important roles in memory that can be independent of their hippocampal inputs.
source_text: They show that the MBs have important roles in memory that can be independent of their hippocampal inputs

claim: The results highlight the importance of the VTNg for mammillary body function.

claim: MTT and VTNg lesions result in strikingly similar spatial memory impairments.
source_text: Not only do MTT and VTNg lesions result in strikingly similar spatial memory impairments

claim: These findings highlight the importance of looking beyond the hippocampus to larger networks of brain regions that contribute to memory.
